es: Extraer de una nota de voz larga la decisión, la petición (también la implícita) y lo prescindible, apoyándote en marcadores de resumen y leyendo entre líneas.

vocabulary.es: en fin, a lo que iba

teaching.en: She tends to go off on a tangent about the traffic, but, anyway, the upshot is that we leave on Friday morning.
teaching.es: Suele irse por las ramas con el tráfico, pero, en fin, lo esencial es que salimos el viernes por la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Go off on a tangent es desviarse del tema; anyway vuelve a lo principal y the upshot is that da la conclusión.
segments: She tends to go off on a tangent about the traffic,
but, anyway, the upshot is that we leave on Friday morning.
teaching.audioText: She tends to go off on a tangent about the traffic, but, anyway, the upshot is that we leave on Friday morning.

teaching.en: Basically, Dad has decided, and all we have to do now is book the tickets by Tuesday, preferably the cheaper ones.
teaching.es: Básicamente, papá ya ha decidido y lo único que tenemos que hacer ahora es reservar los billetes antes del martes, mejor los más baratos.
teaching.explanationEs: Basically resume: primero la decisión, después la tarea. Book significa aquí reservar.
segments: Basically, Dad has decided, and all we have to do now
is book the tickets by Tuesday, preferably the cheaper ones.
teaching.audioText: Basically, Dad has decided, and all we have to do now is book the tickets by Tuesday, preferably the cheaper ones.

teaching.en: You can skip anything she mentions in passing, such as the traffic, because it changes neither the plan nor your own task.
teaching.es: Puedes saltarte todo lo que menciona de pasada, como el tráfico, porque no cambia ni el plan ni tu propia tarea.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo prescindible es lo que no altera ni la decisión ni tu tarea. In passing indica que se dice sin darle importancia.
segments: You can skip anything she mentions in passing, such as the
traffic, because it changes neither the plan nor your own task.
teaching.audioText: You can skip anything she mentions in passing, such as the traffic, because it changes neither the plan nor your own task.

teaching.en: I wonder whether anyone has a spare key, which from her is not idle curiosity but a request disguised as a question.
teaching.es: Me pregunto si alguien tiene una llave de repuesto, lo que en su boca no es simple curiosidad, sino una petición disfrazada de pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: I wonder whether… suele ser una petición disimulada: espera que alguien se ofrezca.
segments: I wonder whether anyone has a spare key, which from her
is not idle curiosity but a request disguised as a question.
teaching.audioText: I wonder whether anyone has a spare key, which from her is not idle curiosity but a request disguised as a question.

teaching.en: When she says it would be great if someone called the hotel, that is a hint, so learn to read between the lines and act.
teaching.es: Cuando dice que sería estupendo que alguien llamara al hotel, eso es una insinuación, así que aprende a leer entre líneas y actúa.
teaching.explanationEs: La petición implícita no usa please ni can you, pero espera una acción. Read between the lines es captar lo no dicho.
segments: When she says it would be great if someone called the hotel, that
is a hint, so learn to read between the lines and act.
teaching.audioText: When she says it would be great if someone called the hotel, that is a hint, so learn to read between the lines and act.

teaching.en: The gist of the voice note is simple: long story short, the flight has changed and we need a new plan by tonight.
teaching.es: La idea general de la nota de voz es sencilla: resumiendo, el vuelo ha cambiado y necesitamos un plan nuevo para esta noche.
teaching.explanationEs: The gist es lo que queda si quitas los detalles; long story short anuncia un resumen.
segments: The gist of the voice note is simple: long story short, the
flight has changed and we need a new plan by tonight.
teaching.audioText: The gist of the voice note is simple: long story short, the flight has changed and we need a new plan by tonight.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión (the upshot) del mensaje.

choices.text: The taxi driver recommended a hotel in Portugal.
They will spend the night at the aunt's house.
They will keep looking for a hotel tonight.

feedback.es: Tras anyway, the upshot is that… llega la conclusión: dormirán en casa de la tía; lo demás es relato previo.

hint.es: Busca lo que sigue a «the upshot is that».

origin.text: I spent ten minutes looking for the hotel, and then the taxi driver told me about his holiday in Portugal. Anyway, the upshot is that we are sleeping at my aunt's house tonight, and I wonder whether someone could tell Grandma.

prompt.es: Completa: «Básicamente, solo hay que reservar los asientos antes de que suban.»

feedback.es: Book también es un verbo: reservar una plaza, un billete o una mesa; reserve es la versión más formal.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa reservar una plaza.

origin.text: Forget the details of the trip. Basically, we just need to ___ the seats before the prices go up.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases pide algo de forma implícita?

choices.text: We are getting to the station at six, and the train leaves at seven.
Someone drove us to the station last week, which was very kind.
It would be great if someone could drive us to the station at six.

feedback.es: It would be great if someone could… deja que alguien se ofrezca: pide una acción sin please ni can you.

hint.es: Una petición implícita espera que alguien se ofrezca.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea principal de la nota.

choices.text: The concert will take place on another day and in another place.
The concert is cancelled and the tickets will be refunded.
The tickets sold out, so the concert moved to Sunday.

feedback.es: Tras the upshot is viene la conclusión: cambian el día y el lugar; la historia de las entradas se puede saltar.

origin.audio: You can skip the long story about the tickets, because the upshot is simple: the concert has moved to Sunday, and it will now be held in the town hall. Oh, and by the way, I wonder whether someone could tell the band.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué espera realmente la persona.

choices.text: That someone buys new plants before she returns.
That someone looks after the plants while she is away.
That someone explains why the plants looked so sad last summer.

feedback.es: I wonder whether anyone could… es una petición disimulada: quiere que alguien cuide las plantas durante su ausencia.

origin.audio: We're off for two weeks, and I wonder whether anyone could water the plants while we're away. I'm not asking anyone specific; it's just that the heat last summer ruined most of them, and they're very dear to me.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión de la nota con su significado.

pairs.es: entender lo que no se dice

feedback.es: Reconocer la expresión te dice si lo que sigue es conclusión, desvío o mensaje implícito.

pairs.es: entender lo que no se dice

prompt.es: Escucha la nota de Tom y completa la ficha: decisión, petición y detalle prescindible.

feedback.es: La decisión y la petición van tras los marcadores; el comentario del café va tras By the way y es prescindible.

sentences: The request: someone should bring the ___.
You can skip: the ___ at the station is terrible.
origin.audio: Hi, it's Tom. I'm calling from the station, where the board says our train to the coast has been cancelled, which is annoying, but not the point. By the way, the coffee here is terrible. Anyway, the upshot is that we leave on Friday at nine instead of Thursday evening, so nobody needs to cancel anything. I wonder whether someone could bring the map, since my phone battery will be flat by then. Oh, and I'd love a sandwich, but that's up to you.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender Tom cuando dice que le encantaría un sándwich?

choices.text: That he has already eaten and needs nothing.
That he will buy one himself at the station.
That he would like someone to bring him one, without asking directly.

feedback.es: «I'd love a sandwich, but that's up to you» es una insinuación: no lo pide de forma directa, pero espera que alguien se lo lleve.

origin.audio: Hi, it's Tom. I'm calling from the station, where the board says our train to the coast has been cancelled, which is annoying, but not the point. By the way, the coffee here is terrible. Anyway, the upshot is that we leave on Friday at nine instead of Thursday evening, so nobody needs to cancel anything. I wonder whether someone could bring the map, since my phone battery will be flat by then. Oh, and I'd love a sandwich, but that's up to you.

prompt.es: Lee la nota y elige el dato que puedes saltarte sin perder la decisión ni la petición.

choices.text: The stall next to theirs was selling cakes.
The deadline of Thursday for the tables.
The idea of asking the school to lend them.

feedback.es: La anécdota de las tartas es un desvío; el plazo y la posibilidad de pedirlas al colegio forman la petición.

origin.text: Hi all, it's Mia. I was at the market this morning, and the stall next to ours was selling cakes, which was funny, because nobody there seemed to know what a cake costs. Long story short, we need two more tables by Thursday, and I wonder whether the school could lend us some.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En fin, lo esencial es que quedamos en la estación.»

answer.text: Anyway, the upshot is that we meet at the station

feedback.es: Anyway vuelve al tema principal y the upshot is that introduce la conclusión con sujeto y verbo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender el hablante sobre la abuela.

choices.text: That she is upset about the change of plans.
That she would actually like a visit from everyone.
That she will send someone to collect them on Sunday.

feedback.es: «Knowing her» indica que lo dicho no es lo que quiere: lo que desea es que vaya toda la familia.

origin.audio: Anyway, the gist is that Grandma cannot travel this year, so we will visit her on Sunday instead. She insisted that we shouldn't make trouble, which, knowing her, means she would love us to bring the whole family.

prompt.es: Lee la nota de Leo: ¿qué espera que haga el grupo, aunque no lo pida?

choices.text: Start the workshop without him at six.
Go to his car and bring the keys.
Find out whether the caretaker has a spare set.

feedback.es: Does anyone know whether…? es una petición implícita de ayuda; el taller empieza a las seis igualmente.

origin.text: Hi, it's Leo. I cannot find the keys to the hall, and I suspect I left them in the car, which is miles away. Does anyone know whether the caretaker has a spare set? Anyway, the workshop starts at six.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se pregunta si alguien podría prestarle un coche más grande el fin de semana.»

feedback.es: Después de wonder, una pregunta indirecta se introduce con whether o if.

origin.text: She never asks directly. Instead, she says she wonders ___ anyone could lend her a bigger car for the weekend.
